title: Chemex brewing guide
scope: Manual six-cup Classic Chemex with compatible bonded paper; app-authored 30 g coffee and 480 g brew-water starting point. Three-cup and named roaster recipes are separate variants.

sources.title: Six Cup Classic CHEMEX: specification and How to Use
supports: Six-cup compatible papers FP-1, FC-100, FS-100, FSU-100
Medium-coarse grind, three layers at spout, gentle pouring below rim
Manufacturer bloom is about 30 seconds; not our exact mass recipe

sources.title: Three Cup Classic CHEMEX: specification and How to Use
supports: Three-cup uses FP-2/FP-2N half-moon paper
Product lists 15 Ounce / 1 Pint inconsistently; no exact conversion inferred

sources.title: How to brew with CHEMEX: FP-1 folding video description
supports: Fold full circle twice; open cone with three layers toward spout and one opposite
Keep spout available as an air channel
Links separate FP-2 folding demonstration

sources.title: Filter Series Info and Support
supports: Larger bonded papers differ from three-cup half-moon paper
Thick side at spout supports paper and helps prevent sealing
Medium-coarse starting grind and disposal of spent paper

sources.title: CHEMEX FAQ
supports: Rinsing is optional; discard rinse water
Slow flow can arise from fine grounds or a sealed spout
Rapid flow may require finer grind

sources.title: Classic Series Info and Support
supports: Brand cup is five ounces; capacities depend on model
Bump is full mark for three-cup and halfway for five- to ten-cup
Remove collar and rawhide before washing, secure dishwasher glass, do not microwave

sources.title: Brew Guide: Chemex
supports: Published eight-cup 42 g / 700 g example
150 g bloom; 450 g cumulative at 45 seconds; 700 g at 105 seconds
About 205 F water and roughly four-minute/volume removal, not this app's six-cup sequence

sources.title: How to Make Chemex Coffee
supports: Published 36-46 g / 600 g example, 200-210 F, medium-coarse grind
80 g bloom; 45-second first interval and 300/400/500/600 g cumulative main pours
Allow full drawdown; 270-330 seconds refers to its published batch

sources.title: Encore ESP Operations Manual, January 2023 v1.0, page 5
supports: Encore ESP manufacturer Chemex starting setting 30
Adjust for recipe and taste; setting is not a universal range
Unplug before grinder cleaning

sources.title: Chemex Six-Cup For One (recipe content unavailable)
supports: Access observation only: the URL returned site navigation without recipe instructions; no recipe claim is supported.

recipe.name: Everyday six-cup Chemex: 30 g / 480 g
equipment: Matching bonded paper: FP-1, FC-100, FS-100, or FSU-100
recipe.grind_description: Medium-coarse, visibly granular rather than powder; no universal grinder number.

expected_time_s.clock_start: First brewing water contacts coffee; preparation and rinse excluded
expected_time_s.clock_end: No standing water remains above the bed and continuous flow has become occasional drips

recipe.completion_signal: Water above the grounds has drained; main flow has slowed to occasional drips. Remove the filter without waiting for every last drip.

steps.instruction: Open matching paper with three layers toward the spout and one opposite; leave the spout groove open.
steps.why: Air needs an escape route as brewed coffee enters the carafe.
steps.completion: Paper fits the six-cup funnel and the spout channel remains clear.

steps.instruction: Wet the paper with hot water, discard the rinse, and put the brewer on a stable scale.
steps.why: Our optional preparation warms the glass and wets the paper; rinse is separate from recipe water.
steps.completion: Paper is wet and no rinse water remains in the carafe.

steps.instruction: Add 30 g medium-coarse coffee, level the bed gently, and tare the scale with everything in place.
steps.why: A consistent weighed dose makes this chosen ratio repeatable.
steps.completion: Level coffee bed and scale reads zero before brewing.

steps.instruction: At first water contact start the timer, pour 90 g evenly, gently stir only if needed to wet dry pockets, and wait until 45 seconds elapsed.
steps.why: Wet the whole bed before the main pours. The 90 g and 45 seconds are app-selected, not a Chemex manufacturer recipe.
steps.completion: All grounds wetted and timer reaches 45 seconds from first water contact, including the pour.

steps.instruction: At 45 seconds pour 150 g gently over the coffee to reach 240 g total. Pause whenever liquid rises too quickly.
steps.why: This app-selected checkpoint divides the remaining water into manageable additions.
steps.completion: Scale reads 240 g cumulative; liquid remains comfortably below both rims.

steps.instruction: When the level has visibly fallen, add the final 240 g gradually to reach 480 g total; divide this addition further if needed for headroom.
steps.why: Flow and safe liquid level determine pace; no unsupported fixed pour-start time.
steps.completion: Scale reads 480 g cumulative, without overflow or sealing the spout.

steps.instruction: Observe drainage and record elapsed time when standing water disappears and the continuous flow becomes occasional drips.
steps.why: Completion follows drainage. This untested 30/480 batch has no independently verified finish window.
steps.completion: No standing water above the bed; main flow has become occasional drips.

steps.instruction: Carefully remove the wet filter, gently swirl the collected coffee, and serve using the collar or handle.
steps.why: Mix the collected coffee and protect hands from hot glass.
steps.completion: Filter removed and coffee served safely.

variants.name: Three-cup half-moon setup
variants.how_it_differs: Use FP-2 or FP-2N. App-selected smaller example: 20 g coffee, 320 g water, 60 g bloom, then 100 g to 160 g cumulative and 160 g to 320 g cumulative. Recheck safe fill and drainage; do not scale a timer.

variants.name: Stumptown published 42/700
variants.how_it_differs: Eight-cup equipment, 150 g bloom, then 450/700 g cumulative at 45/105 seconds, approximately 96 C water, and roughly four-minute/volume removal. This is distinct from app chemex_42_700.

variants.name: Blue Bottle published 600 g
variants.how_it_differs: 36-46 g dose, 80 g bloom, then 300/400/500/600 g cumulative and full drawdown. Its own finish guidance is 270-330 seconds; do not apply it automatically to smaller batches.

variants.name: Encore ESP grind anchor
variants.how_it_differs: Manufacturer suggests setting 30 as the starting point on the Encore ESP only; tune for taste and actual drainage.

troubleshooting.symptom: Slow or stalled flow, liquid rising
troubleshooting.check_first: Stop adding water; inspect correct paper fit and a clear spout groove.
troubleshooting.adjustment: If airflow is clear, try a slightly coarser grind next brew.

troubleshooting.symptom: Fast drainage with thin or sharply sour coffee
troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm even wetting, dose, cumulative water and filter fit.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Try slightly finer next brew; change one variable.

troubleshooting.symptom: Balanced flavor but weaker than desired
troubleshooting.check_first: Verify dose and total water; distinguish strength preference from stalled drainage.
troubleshooting.adjustment: App-authored adjustment informed by Chemex's suggestion to use more coffee for a stronger drink: increase coffee slightly while keeping water fixed.

troubleshooting.symptom: Harsh taste after unusually slow drainage
troubleshooting.check_first: Check spout airflow and pouring before assuming grind is the cause.
troubleshooting.adjustment: With airflow clear, try slightly coarser next brew and compare taste; do not invent an early-removal time.

safety: Keep the brewer stable and liquid below both the paper and glass rims; pause pouring if needed.
Handle hot coffee carefully and hold the brewer by collar or handle rather than hot glass.
Let the carafe cool before washing. Remove wood collar and rawhide; handwash with warm soapy water or secure bare glass in the dishwasher.
Do not reheat a Chemex in a microwave.
If cleaning an electric grinder, unplug it and follow its own manual.

uncertainties: The selected 30/480 recipe has not been physically brewed; no verified batch-specific time or beverage yield is supplied.
Dose/water masses may be changed proportionally, but paper fit, bed depth, pour pacing, airflow and drainage require revalidation.
Three-cup official listing says 15 Ounce / 1 Pint, an inconsistent unit equivalence; no exact converted capacity is used.
George Howell's older six-cup-for-one page returned navigation without recipe content; excluded from recipe evidence.
SRC-SCHMIEDER-FLOW did not resolve to a primary document in inspected guide records; its identity and Chemex applicability remain unverified.
Static catalog and copy review do not establish translation quality, UI execution or kitchen performance.
do_not_claim: The app's six-cup chemex_42_700 sequence is Chemex's official or Stumptown's exact recipe.
The manufacturer requires filter rinsing or a 45-second bloom.
Three-cup Chemex accepts the same folded sheets as the six-cup.
All Chemex sizes have one input-water capacity or one finish time.
The glass bump always marks the same volume or always half capacity.
480 g input water is 480 g beverage or exactly 480 ml water.
Chemex retains a universal 2 g water per gram coffee.
A clock alert proves drawdown is complete.
A given flavor or grinder number works for every bean, roast, water and grinder.
Paper filtration removes all acidity or prevents bitter coffee.
